ACT_1.secondary: Eight months before the accident, the lead locomotive goes to the repair shop after an engine failure. (LM-20)
Given the time and cost of a standard repair, and the pressure to return the locomotive to service, the engine is repaired with an epoxy-like polymeric material. (LM-21)
Its mounting bolt is over-tightened during that repair. The bearing fractures, oil to the valve train falls away, and oil begins accumulating where it should not. (LM-22, LM-23)
72 Class 111 tank cars of petroleum crude, loaded at New Town, North Dakota. 7.7 million litres. (LM-01, LM-02)

ACT_1.label: Tons. 72 loaded tank cars, a buffer box car, five head-end locomotives and a VB car. (LM-39)

ACT_1.secondary: Operated by a single locomotive engineer, under single-person train operations special instructions. (LM-41)
The train stops at the designated crew change point, parked on a descending grade on the main track, just over seven miles from Lac-Megantic. (LM-03, LM-04)

ACT_4.secondary: The TSB identified eighteen. A system with eighteen failure points does not have a villain; it has a design. (LM-24)
MMA developed one in 2002, did not begin implementing it until 2010, and by 2013 it was still not functioning effectively. (LM-26)
Transport Canada's Quebec office did not audit that system until 2010, and does not validate a railway's special instructions or say how many hand brakes a train needs. (LM-27, LM-30)

The crude was classified Packing Group III - the least dangerous option - when it should have been Packing Group II. High vapour pressure and low flashpoint made it readily ignitable. (LM-102, LM-103)

_readme: EVERY CARD CARRIES ITS LEDGER ROW ID. A card sits on screen longer than a sentence is spoken and
reads as the film's own voice, so none of them asserts anything the ledger does not.
REWRITTEN AFTER CHECKING AGAINST THE LEDGER. The first draft was written from general knowledge
of the case and was vague exactly where the record is sharp -- it said 'the number is the case'
instead of the triple that IS the case: SEVEN applied (LM-43), TEN required by MMA's own
ten-per-cent-plus-two formula (LM-44), SEVENTEEN to TWENTY-SIX actually needed (LM-10).
THE BIBLE'S FIRST WARNING IS LOAD-BEARING: do not make the engineer the villain. Three men were
charged and a jury acquitted all three. So ACT_4 leads with EIGHTEEN CAUSES AND CONTRIBUTING
FACTORS (LM-24) and carries LM-25 -- the TSB could NOT conclude a second crew member would have
prevented it -- which blocks the easiest false moral in the story. ACT_5 then does the harder
thing: it states the acquittal AND the six guilty pleas under the Railway Safety Act (LM-77-79),
because 'acquitted' on its own is not what the record says.
TWO CARDS EXIST TO STOP THE AUDIENCE IMAGINING FOOTAGE WE DELIBERATELY DID NOT MAKE: ACT_3's
